Q: doing a linear search python code for a list and for some reason im getting both conditions satisfied, can someone help me with this A:

The loop goes through every item in then list before Search is found. When you enter 15, your program goes through the all elements of the list before 15. The only item before 15 is 30, so before returning Match found for 15, it returns Match not found.

Similarly, 54 is the 10th item in your list, so your program prints Match not found 9 times, and Match found on the tenth.

Don't print Match not found until the last element of the list has been reached:

K = [30,15,25,50,40,35,44,49,55,54]

Search = int(input("Enter the value you want to search: "))
Index = 0
Found = False

while Index<=9 and not Found:
    if K[Index]==Search:
        print("Match found")
        Found=True
    else:
        if Index==9:
            print("Match not found")
        Index=Index+1

Still a linear search.

Or just don't linear search:

print('Found!' if Search in K else 'Not found.')

Q: Can't enter any guesses in this guessing game made in python A:

Show the full code. I made up guess_count and secret_word:

guess_limit = 3
out_of_guesses = False
secret_word = 'kite'
guess_count = 1
guess = input("Enter guess: ").lower()
while guess != secret_word and not (out_of_guesses):
    if guess_count < guess_limit:
        guess = input("Enter guess: ").lower()
        guess_count += 1
    else:
        out_of_guesses = True
if out_of_guesses:
    print("Out Of Guesses, You Lose! ")
else:
    print("You win!")

No way to know what you actually wanted to do. Here's a guess:

from random import choice

guess_limit = 3
out_of_guesses = False

guess_count = 1

secret_word = choice(['password','kite','name','foul','wire','name','locker','computer','mud','wolf','fox','pliers','piano','chair','monk'])

guess = input("Enter guess: ").lower()

while guess != secret_word and not out_of_guesses:
    if guess_count < guess_limit:
        guess = input("Enter guess: ").lower()
        guess_count += 1
        out_of_guesses = False
    else:
        out_of_guesses = True

if out_of_guesses:
    print("Out Of Guesses, You Lose! ")
else:
    print("You win!")

Your booleans were mixed up too. This is guesswork.

Q: How to build strong fundamentals of programming without using AI A:

First, learn the basic syntax and data types - use platforms like W3Schools. Use AI to understand how the syntax works, how the control flows in code. I would suggest some books but I have never read any myself to recommend them.

After that, try some tutorials to understand basic coding styles and practices. And the main part is to build a project. Only a project can show which code is usefull and where to each pattern.

You can always use AI, but before copy pasting code you should know what code it is. For me, if I know what I am copy pasting, I just looks at it. If it seems correct, I use it. If I am not familiar with it, I ask further questions to understand it. Then I write the code myself by looking at the code instead of copy-pasting it.
Don't jump into AI tools like Cursor or Antigravity at the beginning. In your case using the browser to ask AI is better for now.
You got to accept the hard way if you really want to learn.

Q: Typeerror on rabbitmq admin page A:

We had the same problem. Somehow the default vhost '/' was not existing anymore. After opening the management console and adding the vhost '/' under Admin -> Virtual Hosts -> Add a new virtual host, everything was working again. RabbitMQ even recovered all queues, exchanges and messages.

Q: How to use __str__ function to return a string representation of a class A:

Here is an example:

def __str__(self):
    return f'({self.self.country},{self.self.code},{self.self.product}, {self.cost},{self.quantity })'

This way, when you assign values to a class, you can print its string representation

print(new_shoe)

More info here https://www.pythontutorial.net/python-oop/python-str/

Q: importing dictionary from python file to another A:

You haven't made the dictionary dic anywhere, you have made dictionary dic1. In File2, you are import dic1 (the empty dict), not dic. Change File1 to this:

dic1 = {}
dic1['abcd'] = 4
print(dic1)
